prompt: Judge a round of rock-paper-scissors: given the two players' choices, return "a" if player a wins, "b" if player b wins, or "tie".
explanation: Handling the tie first with a.equals(b) removes three of the nine cases immediately -- always compare strings with equals, never ==. After that, only three specific combinations mean player a wins, which one boolean expression can capture; every remaining case must be a win for b. Eliminating cases early keeps branching logic short and readable.
hints: Compare strings with equals, not ==. Start with: if (a.equals(b)) return "tie";
After the tie is gone, list the exact three combinations where a wins.
If it is not a tie and a did not win, the only possibility left is "b".
